newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST - Swedish Riksbank seen not cutting repo - RP.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Swedish Riksbank seen not cutting repo - RP.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, was expected to leave its key repurchase rate unchanged at its regular weekly tender on Tuesday because the crown was too soft, a Reuter poll of 10 economists showed.

All economists agreed that the Riksbank would not cut rates as the crown has softened about five percent since October last year on worries that Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) will not start as planned on January 1, 1999.

The crown has also been hurt by signals that Sweden's minority Social Democratic government might return to traditional party policies, which usually include large public spending, to regain voter support ahead of elections in 1998.

But the economists disagreed about whether the repo had bottomed out with three of the 10 expecting the Riksbank's next move to be a rate hike around year-end, while the others forecast continued cuts.
"There is still room for cuts, on condition that the crown strengthens," said Knut Hallberg, an economist at Swedbank .
"If inflation continues to surprise us in a positive way, we can see a bottom of 3.75 percent in the second quarter.
Inflation has been lower than expected for the past six months with February inflation showing a year-on-year fall of 0.4 percent.
The Riksbank cut the repo 25 times in 1996 to its current level of 4.10 percent, from 8.91 percent, but has not made a move thus far in 1997.
Those believing in a cut expect it to happen after the government has presented its spring budget proposal on April 15.
But a crown strengthening is necessary for the Riksbank to keep easing, economists said.
"We think the crown must come down to at least 119 on the TCW index before the Riksbank can cut," said Marie Giertz, an economist at Handelsbanken.

On Monday, the crown was trading around a TCW index of 122 in real terms. The Riksbank sees the appropriate crown level at a nominal interval of between 110 and 119 on the TCW index, corresponding to an interval of 109-118 in real terms.

The Riksbank's latest quarterly inflation report, released on March 20, did not prompt economists to adjust their forecasts much. In the report, the Riksbank cut its inflation forecast for 1997 to 0.5 percent from 1.5 percent.
"Much of the report was as expected, but it was surprising that they were so keen on downplaying the importance of the crown's current weakness," said Thomas Lindberg at Ohmans
